title: Ravensgate rate-shopping engine

act2.summary: tanager signs a small-parcel arrangement - a new national-zone eligibility exception, unaffected by weight caps, speed tiers or discounts

solutions.title: One shared function decides whether a carrier is even in the running
solutions.tradeoff: This route bet that zone-and-weight eligibility was the pressure most likely to grow a new exception, and pulled both checks into one function shared by both entry points. Tanager's small-parcel exception arrives on exactly that axis: one new clause, inside a function that already receives every value it needs, at 2 lines in a single hunk.

solutions.title: One shared function decides the price, after each carrier's negotiated rate
solutions.tradeoff: This route bet that the per-carrier discount arithmetic was worth insulating first - a reasonable bet, since discount rates are the kind of thing a sales team renegotiates on its own schedule. The small-parcel exception never touches pricing at all: eligibility-by-zone was never pulled out, so it still duplicates the new clause across both entry points, at exactly the no-pattern baseline's cost.

reviewFocus: Does the reader's own restructuring name, honestly, which pressure it chose to relieve - eligibility, or pricing - and admit the other is still duplicated?
Would a reader who restructured pricing instead of eligibility still recognize, from the measured numbers alone, why the small-parcel exception landed cheaply or expensively?
Does the WALKTHROUGH.md for the losing route say plainly that its bet didn't pay off for this act 2, without pretending its own restructuring was worthless in general?
Do both routes agree, byte for byte, with src/ on every act-1 outcome before the exception exists?
For a kata that ships without tests: does the reader's own safety net actually exercise the zone, weight and speed-tier boundaries - or only the happy path?
